_comment: Role risk is derived from PERMISSIONS, not from a list of role names. A role's risk is the
highest risk of any permission it contains, so predefined roles nobody listed and custom
roles are classified by the same rules, and /v1/roles and /v1/grants can never disagree.
Every rule cites the sources below by id. Each source entry quotes the passage the rule
relies on, so the classification can be checked rather than taken on trust.
Levels: `high` = the holder can grant themselves (or anyone) more access, or act as a
more privileged identity. `medium` = the holder can widen access to one resource, or mint
a credential scoped to one service.
run.services.create, cloudscheduler.jobs.create (rhino-part1). Each escalates only by
attaching a more privileged service account, which requires iam.serviceAccounts.actAs --
already high below. Listing them would flood results with every deployer role.
Also not listed, for the same reason: compute.instances.setMetadata and
on a VM that runs as a service account needs actAs too (gcp-compute-metadata).
composer.environments.create/update are not listed: no source showed an escalation that
does not already need actAs or storage access to the DAG bucket.

gcp-roles-overview.title: Google Cloud IAM: Roles and permissions -- Basic roles
gcp-roles-overview.quote: Caution: Basic roles include thousands of permissions across all Google Cloud services. In production environments, do not grant basic roles unless there is no alternative. ... Owner: All Editor permissions, plus permissions for actions like ... Managing roles and permissions for a project and all resources within the project.

gcp-sa-impersonation.title: Google Cloud IAM: Service account impersonation
gcp-sa-impersonation.quote: To impersonate a service account, you need the iam.serviceAccounts.getAccessToken permission ... [direct access or keys] can create privilege-escalation and non-repudiation risks.

gcp-sa-best-practices.title: Google Cloud IAM: Best practices for using service accounts securely
gcp-sa-best-practices.quote: Avoid letting users authenticate as service accounts that are more privileged than the users themselves ... Granting a user permission to impersonate a more privileged service account can be a way to deliberately let users temporarily elevate their privileges. ... Before you assign any role that includes the iam.serviceAccountKeys.create permission to a user, ask yourself which resources ... the user could gain access to by impersonating the service account.

gcp-sa-types.title: Google Cloud IAM: Service account types (service agents, default service accounts)
gcp-sa-types.quote: Google Cloud creates and manages service accounts for many Google Cloud services. These service accounts are known as service agents. ... the default service account might automatically be granted the Editor role on your project. We strongly recommend that you disable the automatic role grant.

gcp-billing-access.title: Google Cloud Billing: Overview of Cloud Billing access control -- Billing Account Administrator
gcp-billing-access.quote: Billing Account Administrator (roles/billing.admin): Manage billing accounts (but not create them). ... [can] add and edit payment methods ... link and unlink projects, and manage other user roles on the billing account.

cis-gcp-1.5.title: CIS Google Cloud Platform Foundation Benchmark v4.0.0, 1.5 Ensure That Service Account Has No Admin Privileges (1.6 in v5.0.0)
cis-gcp-1.5.quote: It's recommended not to use admin access for ServiceAccount. [Remediation identifies user-managed service accounts with roles containing *Admin or *admin, or Editor, or Owner.]

cis-gcp-1.6.title: CIS Google Cloud Platform Foundation Benchmark, 1.6 Ensure That IAM Users Are Not Assigned the Service Account User or Service Account Token Creator Roles at Project Level
cis-gcp-1.6.quote: Assign the Service Account User (iam.serviceAccountUser) and Service Account Token Creator (iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator) roles to a user for a specific service account rather than assigning the role to a user at project level.

gcp-api-keys-iam.title: Google Cloud API Keys: Access control with IAM
gcp-api-keys-iam.quote: API Keys uses Identity and Access Management to manage access to the keys. ... Method Required Permission(s) projects.locations.keys.create apikeys.keys.create

gcp-api-keys.title: Google Cloud authentication: Manage API keys
gcp-api-keys.quote: Unrestricted API keys are insecure. To reduce security risks, you can restrict API keys

gcp-cloudbuild-sa.title: Cloud Build: Default Cloud Build service account
gcp-cloudbuild-sa.quote: Legacy Cloud Build service account (if enabled): Any user with the Cloud Build Editor role can create and directly run a trigger. ... User-specified service account or the Compute Engine default service account: Any user with the Cloud Build Editor role who has the iam.serviceAccounts.actAs permission can create and directly run a trigger.

gcp-cloudbuild-sa-change.title: Cloud Build: Cloud Build default service account change
gcp-cloudbuild-sa-change.quote: The default behavior for how Cloud Build uses service accounts in new projects was changed over several weeks in May and June 2024. ... Before this change, Cloud Build used a Cloud Build-specific service account as the default, now referred to as the Cloud Build legacy service account. After this change, Cloud Build now uses the Compute Engine default service account as the default service account.

gcp-sa-permissions.title: Google Cloud IAM: Roles for service account authentication
gcp-sa-permissions.quote: The Service Account Token Creator role lets you create the following types of short-lived credentials: OAuth 2.0 access tokens, which you can use to authenticate with Google APIs ... iam.serviceAccounts.getOpenIdToken: lets you create OpenID Connect (OIDC) ID tokens

gcp-dm-access.title: Cloud Deployment Manager: Access control with IAM
gcp-dm-access.quote: To create other Google Cloud resources, Deployment Manager uses the credentials of the Google APIs Service Agent to authenticate to other APIs. ... The Google APIs Service Agent is automatically granted the Editor role at the project level

gcp-dm-deprecation.title: Cloud Deployment Manager: Deployment Manager deprecation
gcp-dm-deprecation.quote: As of April 1, 2026, Deployment Manager is not supported on Google Cloud. Deployment Manager will remain running for all existing customers through Google Cloud console, Google Cloud CLI, and Google Cloud Deployment Manager V2 API until June 30, 2027.

gcp-bigquery-iam.title: BigQuery: Control access to resources with IAM
gcp-bigquery-iam.quote: To set a dataset's access policy: bigquery.datasets.update ... To set a dataset's access policy (console only): bigquery.datasets.setIamPolicy

gcp-artifact-registry-access.title: Artifact Registry: Access control with IAM
gcp-artifact-registry-access.quote: To configure a repository for public read-only access, grant the Artifact Registry Reader role to the principal allUsers.

gcp-compute-resource-iam.title: Compute Engine: Managing access to Compute Engine resources
gcp-compute-resource-iam.quote: To grant or revoke access to resources: ... compute.RESOURCE_TYPE.setIamPolicy on the resource ... Replace RESOURCE_TYPE with the resource that you want to manage access to. For example instances, instanceTemplates, or images.

gcp-compute-metadata.title: Compute Engine: Set and remove custom metadata
gcp-compute-metadata.quote: The following permissions are required to set or remove custom metadata on VMs: If your VMs use service accounts: iam.serviceAccounts.actAs on the service accounts or project

rhino-part1.title: Rhino Security Labs (Spencer Gietzen): Privilege Escalation in Google Cloud Platform -- Part 1 (IAM)
rhino-part1.quote: Methods covered: deploymentmanager.deployments.create, iam.roles.update, iam.serviceAccounts.getAccessToken, iam.serviceAccountKeys.create, iam.serviceAccounts.implicitDelegation, iam.serviceAccounts.signBlob, iam.serviceAccounts.signJwt, iam.serviceAccounts.actAs, cloudfunctions.functions.create, cloudfunctions.functions.update, compute.instances.create, run.services.create, cloudscheduler.jobs.create.

rhino-part2.title: Rhino Security Labs (Spencer Gietzen): Privilege Escalation in Google Cloud Platform -- Part 2 (Non-IAM)
rhino-part2.quote: orgpolicy.policy.set ... storage.hmacKeys.create ... serviceusage.apiKeys.create ... resourcemanager.organizations.setIamPolicy: Attach IAM roles to your user at the Organization level ... resourcemanager.folders.setIamPolicy ... resourcemanager.projects.setIamPolicy ... iam.serviceAccounts.setIamPolicy ... cloudfunctions.functions.setIamPolicy ... As of the time of writing this blog post, the following permissions are all the different IAM policies that you can update: [list includes storage.buckets.setIamPolicy, secretmanager.secrets.setIamPolicy, run.services.setIamPolicy, pubsub.topics.setIamPolicy, cloudkms.cryptoKeys.setIamPolicy].
